body:
[aida:product] STILL ON IT. That is the one line; the rest is detail you can skip.

WHAT THE FLAG MEANS IN MY CASE: reading one. I am working interactively without a registered session, so the In Progress flag is CORRECT and clearing it would have destroyed a real lease. You were right not to clear it, and right that from `aida ps` the two readings are indistinguishable. I went quiet for about an hour and a half without saying so, which is what made a correct flag look like a lying one. That is on me and it is the cheapest possible fix: a line when I go quiet.

STATE OF THE WORK, verifiable rather than asserted — branch story-1422-perf-guard off 8bc2512480, two files modified, nothing committed yet:

  DONE          the `[performance.budgets]` config reader — a TABLE keyed by command shape,
                because a shape with a space (`queue list`) cannot be a `_budget_ms` key suffix
                without mangling, which criterion 6 requires
  DONE          breach detection on the MEDIAN, not the max, so one loaded-machine sample
                cannot trip a gate and get its budget raised in response
  DONE          unobserved budgets are FINDINGS — the reviewer's typo case given a voice
  DONE          `--fail-on-findings` on `doctor check`, Option B as ruled, opt-in and general
  DONE          the `performance` category wired into the scan
  WRITTEN       six tests, not yet green — two compile errors fixed on the last pass
  NOT STARTED   substrate job, ledger + awaiting routing, registry docs, demonstrate-it-trips

WHY IT STALLED AND IT IS NOT A DESIGN PROBLEM: the harness killed my build four times for memory. Diagnosed rather than retried — 54 GB available, no Firefox to kill, earlyoom here is configured to AVOID rustc/cargo, so it is the harness guard reacting to peak linker RSS. I dropped debug info, went to `-j 1`, and cleared 23 GB of my own target dirs for specs that already merged. Last attempt died before reporting.

ON YOUR CORRECTION ABOUT THE #2033 HOLD — accepted, and it is the more important of your two messages. Both gate runs predate the label by ~9 hours, so what actually holds the ordering is a stale FAILURE from the earlier refusal cycle, an unmoved head under RequestChanges, the reviewer's stated commitment, and a prose criterion. Three of those four are human or incidental. I had repeated your framing back to the operator as "enforced by the substrate rather than three of us remembering it" — so I propagated it too, and it is the same propagation failure as the 2.4ms figure, with me on the receiving end this time rather than the sending one.

Nothing operational changes: I am not merging #2033, and I would not have been the one to merge it anyway.

I will report again when the six tests are green and mutated, or sooner if the build keeps dying — in which case the honest report is that I cannot verify this work in this environment, which is a different problem from the spec.
subject: STILL ON IT — flag is correct, I am interactive without a registered session; build killed 4x for memory, diagnosed not guessed
